blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Blast block 37633619, the USDB proxy at 0x4300000000000000000000000000000000000003 resolved to implementation 0x4ef0d788470e2feb6559b93075ec5be51dba737d, with bridge() = 0x4300000000000000000000000000000000000005 and REPORTER = L1 USDYieldManager 0xa230285d5683C74935aD14c446e137c8c8828438. The verified implementation exposes ordinary transfer and transferFrom and has no active pause, blacklist, or freeze function; its mint and burn functions are restricted to the L2 bridge, and fixed-block calls from an unrelated account reverted. However, admin() is L2 ProxyAdmin 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018, whose owner is 3-of-5 Safe 0xb9ca260493a0a6f9cfc1c2931faca48ac4af0937 with no enabled modules. The verified ProxyAdmin source permits its owner to replace the USDB implementation, so this known control can make holder transfers or balances restrictable even though the live implementation has no direct blacklist function.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDB's sole authored Blast deployment is a bridge representation whose supply tracks stablecoins escrowed in the Ethereum USDYieldManager and is minted through Blast's dedicated L1BlastBridge/L2BlastBridge pair. Bridge mint/burn, escrow/accounting, administration, and proxy upgrades are route-scoped here and are not native Mint Authority.

routes.reviewNote: Fixed-block reads at Ethereum block 25770239 and Blast block 39052431 resolve the USDYieldManager/L1BlastBridge/L2BlastBridge pair, the L1 and L2 ProxyAdmins, and the two route-owner Safes; this route remains an external lock/mint representation.

controls.label: USDB Ethereum USDYieldManager owner Safe
controls.capDescription: The USDYieldManager and L1BlastBridge route converts deposited stablecoins into DAI-backed bridge accounting; no standalone token cap was observed, and the route's amount bound is the escrow/conversion and paired withdrawal invariant.

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: Approved USDC/USDT/DAI enter the Ethereum USDYieldManager through L1BlastBridge; withdrawals request release from the manager after USDB is burned on Blast.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: At Ethereum block 25770239, USDYieldManager totalValue() was 12940276526476577782191492 WAD and sharePrice() was 1000000000000000000000000000; these are route-level reserve/accounting reads, not a native USDB cap.
routeChecks.caps: No fixed token cap or independent prudential attestor was evidenced; route-level mint capacity follows deposited/conversion accounting and paired bridge finalization.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The 3-of-5 Ethereum Safe owns USDYieldManager and can change its bridge, provider, insurance, and administration configuration; L1 proxy upgrades are separately represented below.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770239 (2026-08-16 21:12:35 UTC), USDYieldManager.owner() returned 0x4f72ee94b8ba3be7f886565d3583a7f636c58b05, a 3-of-5 Gnosis Safe. The Safe had the five owners recorded above, an empty module sentinel, and zero guard/fallback handler reads. The manager's totalValue() and sharePrice() reads establish current route accounting; the Safe's bridge-admin power is preserved here as Bridge Risk rather than native USDB mint authority.

controls.label: USDB Ethereum L1 bridge ProxyAdmin owner Safe
controls.capDescription: L1 ProxyAdmin 0x364289230b8cc7d9120ef962af37ebcfe23ce883 can replace the USDYieldManager and L1BlastBridge implementations, changing the route's escrow, conversion, paired-finalization, or withdrawal constraints without a timelock.

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Ethereum block 25770239, USDYieldManager.getImplementation() returned 0xecddf748a60e23609c07af6ca3856744b139b911, getOwner() returned L1 ProxyAdmin 0x364289230b8cc7d9120ef962af37ebcfe23ce883, and L1BlastBridge resolved to implementation 0x7a2075519dd9598b62075fd397af0dd34b14619a with the same admin. ProxyAdmin.owner() returned the 3-of-5 Safe above; no timelock was evidenced.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770239 (2026-08-16 21:12:35 UTC), L1 ProxyAdmin 0x364289230b8cc7d9120ef962af37ebcfe23ce883 administered both the USDYieldManager and L1BlastBridge implementation paths and its owner() returned the same 3-of-5 Ethereum Safe. The Safe's five signers, empty modules, zero guard/fallback reads, and no-delay upgrade authority are retained here; this is bridge-route upgrade/admin risk, not native-USDB issuance.

controls.label: USDB Blast L2 ProxyAdmin owner Safe
controls.capDescription: Blast ProxyAdmin 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018 can replace the USDB and L2BlastBridge implementations, changing bridge mint/burn, peer pairing, or route-accounting constraints without a timelock.

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Blast block 39052431, USDB's EIP-1967 admin was 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018 with implementation 0x4ef0d788470e2feb6559b93075ec5be51dba737d; L2BlastBridge used the same ProxyAdmin with implementation 0xc0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c3d30005. ProxyAdmin.owner() returned Blast Safe 0xb9ca260493a0a6f9cfc1c2931faca48ac4af0937; no timelock was evidenced.

controls.evidence: At Blast block 39052431 (2026-08-16 21:11:17 UTC), the USDB proxy and L2BlastBridge both used ProxyAdmin 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018, whose owner() returned Blast Safe 0xb9ca260493a0a6f9cfc1c2931faca48ac4af0937. The Safe is 3-of-5 with the five signers recorded above, an empty module sentinel, and zero guard/fallback handler reads; this representation-upgrade authority remains scoreable under Bridge Risk.
